consensus_summary: Across the consensus responses, tzitzit are primarily the tassels or fringes commanded on garment corners as a visual mnemonic to remember and obey all the LORD's commandments and to live holy rather than follow one's own heart and eyes (Num 15:37-41; Deut 22:12). Secondary readings (healing via Jesus' fringe/wings, blue-thread symbolism, ostentation, etc.) are treated as common or minority elaborations that do not displace the explicit primary sense.
book_summary: The tassels bound to the corners of the garment; looking upon them reminds the wearer of all the LORD's commandments, to do them.
consensus_core_identification: Tassels/fringes on garment corners that function as a divinely commanded visual reminder to remember and obey God's commandments.
book_core_identification: Tassels bound to garment corners that, when looked upon, remind the wearer of all the LORD's commandments so as to do them.
rationale: Both the consensus primary meaning and the book entry reduce to the identical core referent and function stated in Numbers 15: the tassels themselves as a reminder of the commandments for the purpose of doing them. Secondary Christological, color, or ostentation readings in the consensus are extras that the book simply does not include; they do not alter or contradict the shared core identification. No boundary cases are added, excluded, or reclassified.
strongest_objection: The book's cross-reference to Wings might be thought to import the secondary Malachi/healing reading into the core, but the printed entry text itself remains strictly the Numbers reminder sense and does not redefine the referent.
